tickets.title: Repair chores/60 archive: old refs, landing conflict check, pending write sets
tickets.what:
Milestone review j1b0f5df80f74cd93 found five majors in the chores/60 ticket archive (commit 4ec0c6b7). Fix all of them in one slice. Keep the 64 KiB cap and the rules chores/60 already set: done/wontfix only, never the highest-numbered ticket, the blocked_by exclusion, one write set under the tickets lock.

1. Landing conflict (`src/mcp/land-runner.ts` ~427-430): the land refuses whenever any ticket moved and the incoming land touched `.hud/objectives.md`, even when the archive needs no Objective change (for example, the target shard is already linked). Refuse only a real conflict: the archive needs to add a Features link and the incoming land changes the same `.hud/objectives.md`. Compare against the incoming Objective contents. Cover the already-linked-shard case.
2. Owner waits (`src/collectors/project-board.ts` ~119-121 and ~531-548): `waitSettled` compares literal IDs, so `(waits on sample/01)` stops matching once the ticket moves to `sample-done/01` and a settled request shows as waiting again. When matching waits, resolve old ticket IDs through the archive family. Do not rewrite owner prose.
3. Flake dispatch (`src/mcp/land-flakes.ts` ~280-287): `inspectRunningListTicket` reads only the named feature and returns `unavailable` when the number is missing, so a wontfix ticket that was archived keeps its flake collection pending forever (`hasPendingFlakeCollection` ~655-668, `src/runtime/work-retention.ts` ~345-346). Use the archive-aware resolver before declaring a ticket unavailable.
4. Stale pending digest (`src/tickets/archive.ts` ~97-108, `src/tickets/commit.ts` ~104-112): after an archive creates a new shard and before the sweep commits it, an ordinary HUD add that links another feature to an Objective rewrites `.hud/objectives.md` outside `prepareTicketWrites`. The pending `@objectives` digest goes stale and the commit path reports a hand edit that never happened. When HUD extends a file that belongs to a pending HUD write group and whose preimage still matches the recorded digest, register the new digest under the same locks. Keep the fence for real hand edits.
5. Ambiguous old refs (`src/tickets/archive.ts` ~55-63, `src/tickets/store.ts` ~238-247): the planner skips a shard that already holds the same number and can move the ticket into a later shard, so the archive family ends up with two copies and `get <feature>/NN` throws as ambiguous. Before moving a candidate, check that its number is unique across the whole archive family. If its old ref would become ambiguous, leave it in the source and try the next candidate.

Also: (a) pull the sibling-match and ambiguity rule, which the CLI, the bounded collector and the store each implement separately, into one shared pure function over already-loaded candidates. Each caller keeps its own I/O bounds. The planner uses the same function to check its proposed destination. (b) Once a write triggers archiving, move every eligible ticket, not just enough to fit. Otherwise the source stays just under 64 KiB and almost every later write reruns the planner across all features. Update docs/reference.md where the archive behaviour it describes changes.

acceptance.text: A cap-crossing land whose target shard is already linked, carrying an unrelated .hud/objectives.md change, lands. A land that would need a new Features link and also edits .hud/objectives.md is still refused. Unit tests cover both.
An owner request `(waits on sample/01)` stays settled after sample/01 moves to sample-done/01 (unit test).
A pending flake dispatch whose wontfix ticket was archived resolves and stops retaining its flow (unit test).

Archive into a new shard, then an ordinary add that links another feature to an Objective: the sweep/commit path commits both and reports no hand edit. A real hand edit of .hud/objectives.md is still fenced. Unit tests cover both.
With sample/01 in the source and sample-done/01 already present, the planner does not move sample/01. `get sample/01` still resolves uniquely (unit test).
One shared matching function serves the CLI, the collector, the store and the planner's destination check.
A cap-crossing write moves every eligible ticket. The next small write to the same feature does not run the archive again (unit test).
Existing chores/60 archive tests still pass. docs/reference.md is updated.

tickets.title: Decision-picked Sonic thinking maps by relative position onto each model's own levels
tickets.live_try: Dispatch a sonic job whose Decision pick is `high` on the qwen3.8-flash preset and on the deepseek preset: job.json shows `thinking: medium` for qwen and `high` for deepseek; a failover from one to the next shows each model's own mapping.
tickets.what: Today `nearestThinking()` (`src/mcp/launch-thinking.ts`) picks by absolute distance on the global 8-level `thinkingOrder`, so the Decision API's four intent levels (`thinking_choices` none/low/high/max in `packages/hud-mcp/roles/sonic.json`) collapse on models with other ladders: on [off, low, medium, high] both high and max become high and medium is never used; on [low..max, ultra] ultra is never used. Also `src/mcp/dispatch/orchestrator.ts` (~1387-1396) writes the mapped value back to `job.thinking`, so a failover to the next candidate maps from the previous model's level instead of the original pick. Fix: keep `nearestThinking` for `thinking_source` `explicit` and `default` (literal level, nearest only when unsupported). For `thinking_source: 'decision'` add `adaptDecisionThinking(picked, supported)`: sort `supported` by `thinkingOrder`, split `hasOff` and `active` (non-off). `none` -> `off` if supported, else `active[0]`. Otherwise intent index k in [low, high, max] (m = 3): no active -> `off`; one active -> `active[0]`; else endpoints aligned, `active[round_up(k * (len - 1) / (m - 1))]` (owner/main 2026-11-27: the middle intent rounds toward the stronger level; thinking follows difficulty). Results: [off, low, medium, high] -> off/low/medium/high; [off, low, high, max] -> off/low/high/max; [low, medium, high, xhigh, max] -> low/low/high/max; [low..max, ultra] -> low/low/xhigh/ultra; [off, high] -> off/high/high/high; [off] -> off. Keep the original Decision pick on the job (e.g. `thinking_pick`) and map from it for every failover candidate; record the mapped level per attempt as today. Read the levels from the existing sources only (pi probe of the model's `thinkingLevelMap`, `cliThinking` in `src/models/models-catalog.json`); no model names in code. Update docs/reference.md where Sonic thinking selection is described.

acceptance.text: Unit tests in tests/unit/model-catalog.test.mjs (or the launch-thinking test) cover every row above plus [off, minimal, low, medium, high]
Unit test: a failover from a [off, low, medium, high] model to a [low..max] model maps the original `high` pick to medium then high, not from the first model's mapped value
Explicit and default thinking still go through nearestThinking unchanged (existing tests pass)

tickets.title: Ticket archive: one archive-aware write path, archive-family replacement lookup, committed hand-edit reconciliation
tickets.what:
Structural repair of the chores/60 ticket archive (follow-up to chores/61). Milestone review j93033c2fe4271edc found three more majors of the same kinds round 1 repaired, so fix the shape, not each case:

1. One write path. Every production ticket writer goes through the archive-aware path under the existing locks: `collectGateFlakes` (`src/mcp/land-flakes.ts` ~466, ~491) and `recordUnattendedAcceptance` (`src/mcp/local-tickets.ts` ~609) currently call `writeTicketFeature` directly, which applies the 64 KiB cap before `prepareTicketWrites` ever runs. Make the cap-checking raw writer unreachable from production callers (private to the store or folded into the archive-aware entry point) so a future writer cannot bypass archiving. Plan the acceptance documents together so one archive's ref rewrites are not overwritten by another preloaded document. A file holding only the protected highest ticket still fails as today.
2. Replacement lookup. `ticketReplacements` (`src/mcp/local-tickets.ts` ~406–419) and `TicketRollup.derive` (`src/collectors/ticket-rollup.ts`, dropped-target branch) resolve `Replaced by <feature>/NN` against the loaded archive family (the same resolution `get` uses), at lookup time. Never rewrite the owner's comment text.
3. Committed hand edit. When a pending HUD write group's member (e.g. `.hud/objectives.md`) no longer matches its digest but is clean and committed in Git, reconcile: retire that member from the group without overwriting or recommitting the owner's bytes, and sweep the remaining matching HUD members as before (`src/tickets/commit.ts` ~77–113, `src/mcp/land-records.ts` ~167–172). Uncommitted mismatches keep the current fence and message.
4. Delete the fallback archive scan in `waitSettled` (`src/collectors/project-board.ts` ~120–142); production passes `ticketsScan.resolve`. Keep literal matching without a resolver; test archive matching through the collector.

Out of scope: archive layout, shard naming, the all-eligible policy chores/61 set, the `.noticed` foreign-claim issue in `src/workflows/events.ts`.
Size: about 150–250 source lines net, 3–4 main-path tests extended in the existing ticket-commit/archive suites.

acceptance.text: A ready ticket whose dependency is a wontfix ticket `Replaced by` a done ticket stays ready after a cap-crossing add archives the replacement (`hud_tickets ready` lists it before and after).

A gate-flake add and an unattended finish on a feature just below 64 KiB with an archivable old done ticket both succeed and archive instead of failing; a feature with only the protected highest ticket still fails with the current error.

tickets.title: Ticket archive: commit archive moves immediately; delete pending write groups; complete-family lookup
tickets.what:
Implement the one-ticket build brief in oracle report jf97748fe19929a56 §3 (read it with `hud_read({job: "jf97748fe19929a56", mode: "full"})`; it is the spec, including the invariants in §2). Main chose candidate A (2026-11-27) after three reviews in a row found majors in the archive (j1b0f5df80f74cd93, j93033c2fe4271edc, jab4c33393980dadd).

In short:
- An archive move is never left pending: when a write would cross 64 KiB, acquire `main-checkout` lease → `tickets` lock → `objective` lock, re-plan from fresh disk state, write all touched files and commit them in one commit (`tickets: archive <feature>`); local `hud_land` folds it into its amended commit. Wait 300 s in `hud_tickets` and `recordUnattendedAcceptance`; `collectGateFlakes` uses 0 and defers to its existing retry. Uncommitted hand edits on any touched file refuse before anything is written; a Git failure restores the pre-write bytes and index.
- Ordinary single-file edits under the cap stay lease-free and Git-free, as today.
- `ticket-writes.json` becomes a flat key → sha256 map. Delete `@groups`, `extendsPendingWriteGroup`, `readReconciledTicketWriteState`, group fencing and the related git-mode helpers.
- `matchArchivedTicket` returns missing when the source feature or any archive sibling is unreadable (or the scan is truncated); `ticket-rollup.ts`, `ticket-store.ts` and `cli/tickets.ts` use it.
- Update `docs/reference.md` (and `.zh`).
Out of scope: the oracle's two separate hardening items, external-tracker archive commits.
Size: net deletion (oracle estimate ~75 added / ~120 removed in src) plus test updates in the ticket commit/store suites. Stop and report if it grows past ~1.5×.

acceptance.text: A non-overflowing add/update stays lease-free and Git-free while a land holds the main-checkout lease.

A cap-crossing add, gate-flake add and unattended finish each commit source, shard, ref rewrites and Objective link in one commit; `git restore` of the shard afterwards keeps the moved tickets retrievable.
A cap-crossing local `hud_land` produces one amended commit and keeps incoming `.hud/objectives.md` rules.
An uncommitted hand edit on any archive-touched file refuses before any file is written.
With `sample.json` or a `sample-done*` sibling unreadable, a dependency `Replaced by sample/NN` stays blocked in `ready` (matching `get`), `waitSettled` stays open, and `hud tickets show` fails.
No `@groups` code remains in src.

tickets.title: Ticket archive repair: staged-edit refusal, receipt-before-rename, legacy @groups fail-closed, Git-probe wording
tickets.what:
Repair four findings from milestone review ja4f8aac10f123f88 (read it: `~/.hud/jobs/ja4f8aac10f123f88/report.md`) against chores/66 (commit f4f6954b). Keep the candidate-A design; do not reintroduce @groups or reconciliation.

1. Staged hand edit (review #1): `inspectMainPath` in `src/tickets/commit.ts` checks only worktree bytes. HUD never leaves staged changes on a ticket file, so for an existing tracked file treat any staged index change (porcelain X column not ' ' and not '?') as a hand edit and refuse before writing. Applies to archive preflight (`checkArchiveFiles`) and to the pending-write sweep (`collectPendingWrites` should skip such a path, not commit over the staged blob).
2. Receipt ordering (review #5): `prepareTicketWrites` in `src/tickets/store.ts` renames the feature file before saving `ticket-writes.json`. Restore the old guarantee: the receipt is saved before any project file is renamed into place (e.g. stage temp files via `writeFileAtomic`'s `beforeRename`, or save the receipt first). If the receipt save fails, no project file changes. No recursive multi-file publisher is needed beyond what that takes.
3. Legacy ledger (review #4): `readTicketWrites` silently drops an old `@groups` key. Fail closed instead: if the ledger has `@groups`, refuse sweep/land/archive with one clear error that names the ledger path and the recovery (commit or revert the listed files by hand, then delete the `@groups` key). Do not restore group reconciliation.
4. Git-free wording (review #2): an ordinary edit to a feature whose digest was already pruned runs a read-only Git probe (`isCleanInGitSync`). Keep that probe (it is the hand-edit guard) and correct `docs/reference.md` / `docs/reference.zh.md` to say ordinary edits take no lease and make no commit, and run only a read-only Git status probe when the file has no recorded HUD digest. Add a test: after a sweep prunes the digest, a small `update` succeeds while a land holds `main-checkout` (lease-free).

Size budget: about 40 added / 10 removed in src plus tests. Stop and report if it grows past 1.5x.

acceptance.text: An owner edit staged on a HUD-pending ticket file, with the worktree reverted to HUD's bytes, makes a cap-crossing add refuse before writing; the staged index blob and the worktree are unchanged afterwards, and `hud_tickets commit` skips that file.
If saving `ticket-writes.json` fails during an ordinary add, the project ticket file is unchanged and the add reports an error (no duplicate ticket on retry).
A ledger carrying a legacy `@groups` key makes `commit`, local `hud_land` record sweep and an archive refuse with a message naming the recovery; no file is committed.

After a sweep prunes a feature's digest, a small `update` succeeds while another holder has the `main-checkout` lease; `docs/reference.md` and `.zh` describe the read-only Git probe instead of claiming no Git execution.
No `@groups` handling beyond the fail-closed check remains in src.

tickets.title: Ticket add: no duplicate on retry after a partial publish or a post-commit cleanup failure
tickets.what:
Review j5e6d4fc01e173396 (hud_read, mode full), two failure paths that need unwritable directories, low priority.
1. An ordinary add publishes the ticket file before writing the Objective `Features` link (`src/tickets/archive.ts` ~129–134, `src/tickets/store.ts` ~399–405); a failure on the second file reports the add as failed and a retry duplicates the ticket. Stage all outputs before publishing the first, or restore the first on failure.
2. `pruneTicketWrites` runs after the archive commit succeeds (`src/tickets/commit.ts` ~164–167); a receipt-cleanup failure reports a committed add as failed, and on local land can record the pre-amend SHA (`land-runner.ts` ~485–499). Return the committed outcome and SHA with a cleanup warning.
Optional: build the publisher only at the ordinary publication site (reviewer's deletion note).
Size: ~40 source lines; two tests (failure writing the second project file → retry creates exactly one ticket with the link; prune failure → returned outcome matches HEAD).

acceptance.text: A failure writing the Objective link leaves no published ticket, and a retry creates exactly one ticket with the link.
A receipt-cleanup failure after a successful archive commit returns success with the committed SHA and a warning.
